entries.definition: A variational lower bound on mutual information formed by adding input entropy to the expected log probability assigned by a normalized conditional decoder to the input given the output.
entries.identity_notes: The Barber–Agakov bound is the mathematical objective, distinct from Barber and Agakov’s alternating IM optimization procedure. It requires a normalized decoder; TUBA and NWJ provide different parameterizations using unnormalized critics. Reconstruction terminology alone does not identify a VAE, a particular autoencoder architecture or the complete IM algorithm. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 208 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 57 lines each: existing MINE-f component discussion, shared primary-source references, and discovery/review context. Four native neighbors and seven exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing relations were inspected.
entries.mechanism: For a joint distribution p(x,y) and normalized conditional decoder q(x|y), define L_BA=H(X)+E_p(x,y)[log q(X|Y)], using differential entropy for continuous variables when the required quantities are finite. The identity I(X;Y)−L_BA=E_p(y)[KL(p(X|Y)||q(X|Y))] gives L_BA<=I(X;Y). Equality holds when the decoder matches the true conditional almost everywhere. For representation learning with fixed p(x), an encoder p_theta(y|x) and decoder q_phi(x|y) can be trained to increase the expected decoder log probability; H(X) is constant with respect to their parameters. Dropping that constant for optimization does not supply a numerical information estimate when the entropy is unknown.

entries.definition: An alternating optimization procedure that adjusts a noisy encoder and a variational decoder to increase the Barber–Agakov lower bound on transmitted information for a fixed input distribution.
entries.identity_notes: This is the named IM algorithm in Barber and Agakov’s 2003 paper, not every algorithm that maximizes information. It is separate from its lower-bound objective and from RIM’s regularized discrete clustering, MINE’s dependence estimation and DIM’s feature-matching framework. The analogy to expectation maximization does not make the optimized target an observed-data likelihood. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 208 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 57 lines each: existing MINE-f component discussion, shared primary-source references, and discovery/review context. Four native neighbors and seven exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing relations were inspected.
entries.mechanism: Choose a fixed input distribution p(x), a parameterized encoder p_theta(y|x), and a class Q of normalized decoders q(x|y) for which the expected decoder log probability is tractable or can be approximated. Starting from an encoder and decoder, hold q fixed and maximize H(X)+E_p(x)p_theta(y|x)[log q(X|Y)] over theta. Then hold theta fixed and fit q within Q by maximizing the same expectation. Repeat the two updates. H(X) is constant in these updates. Exact coordinate maximizations cannot decrease the chosen lower bound; approximate updates require their own improvement check. The paper develops a noisy linear projection with Gaussian decoding as one feature-extraction configuration and also describes richer encoder/decoder choices.

entries.definition: A variational lower bound on Kullback–Leibler divergence that subtracts a product-distribution exponential critic moment from a joint-distribution critic expectation when specialized to mutual information.
entries.identity_notes: NWJ denotes the variational objective, also called the f-GAN KL bound or MINE-f objective in the inspected follow-up. The neural MINE-f estimator is an optimization configuration using this bound, not a separate formula here. The original paper also develops density-ratio estimation algorithms; this record does not equate the mathematical bound with those kernel estimators or with MINE’s Donsker–Varadhan objective. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 208 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 57 lines each: existing MINE-f component discussion, shared primary-source references, and discovery/review context. Four native neighbors and seven exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing relations were inspected.
entries.mechanism: For P absolutely continuous with respect to Q and a real critic T with well-defined expectations, set L_NWJ=E_P[T]−E_Q[exp(T−1)]<=KL(P||Q). The original representation is sup_(g>0){E_P[log g]−E_Q[g]+1}; substituting g=exp(T−1) gives the displayed objective. With P=p(x,y) and Q=p(x)p(y), it lower-bounds I(X;Y). Under positive density ratios and sufficient critic capacity, T*=1+log(dP/dQ) attains equality; boundary cases may require limiting critics. For a fixed critic with integrable moments, correctly sampled empirical means estimate this expected bound without a log-of-sample-mean bias. Optimizing a neural critic changes the statistical estimation and optimization problem and does not inherit convexity merely from the original function-space formulation.

entries.definition: A tractable unnormalized Barber–Agakov lower-bound parameterization that uses a real critic and a positive output-dependent normalizer to replace an intractable log partition term by a linear upper bound.
entries.identity_notes: TUBA is the named parameterization with separate critic f(x,y) and normalizer a(y)>0. It is algebraically NWJ evaluated at T=f−log(a)+1; retaining it separately records its explicit normalizer and optimization interpretation, not a claim of inequivalent unrestricted variational families. Fixing a=e gives NWJ with the same f, while a held-fixed scalar moving average explains the modified MINE gradient. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 208 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 57 lines each: existing MINE-f component discussion, shared primary-source references, and discovery/review context. Four native neighbors and seven exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing relations were inspected.
entries.mechanism: Let Z(y)=E_p(x)[exp(f(X,y))]. For normalized q(x|y)=p(x)exp(f(x,y))/Z(y), the unnormalized Barber–Agakov expression is E_joint[f]−E_p(y)[log Z(y)]. Apply log Z<=Z/a+log a−1 for a(y)>0 to obtain L_TUBA=1+E_joint[f(X,Y)−log a(Y)]−E_product[exp(f(X,Y))/a(Y)]<=I(X;Y). The inequality replacing log Z is tight at a(y)=Z(y); full information tightness additionally requires a critic that represents the conditional-to-marginal relationship. Critic and positive normalizer parameters can be optimized toward the same objective. Reparameterizing T=f−log a+1 recovers exactly the NWJ expression. With fixed functions and appropriate independent joint/product sampling and integrability, the linear expectations admit unbiased Monte Carlo estimates of this bound.

entries.definition: A family of multi-sample mutual-information lower bounds that interpolates the critic’s empirical partition estimate with a positive variational normalizer inside a ratio, connecting NWJ and InfoNCE parameterizations.
entries.identity_notes: This is Poole et al.’s I_alpha family, not Rényi alpha-information, a convex average of final scalar bounds, or an ordinary temperature parameter. Its endpoints connect existing parameterizations; the interior normalizer and residual product expectation define the distinct construction. The paper’s proposed optimal critic is explicitly a conjecture. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 208 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 57 lines each: existing MINE-f component discussion, shared primary-source references, and discovery/review context. Four native neighbors and seven exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing relations were inspected.
entries.mechanism: Draw X_1:K independently from p(x), with Y conditional on X_1 for the joint term. Let m(y;X_1:K)=K^−1 sum_i exp(f(X_i,y)), b_alpha=alpha*m+(1−alpha)*q(y), and r=exp(f(X_1,y))/b_alpha, for q(y)>0 and alpha in [0,1]. Define I_alpha=1+E_p(x_1:K)p(y|x_1)[log r]−E_p(x_1:K)p(y)[r]. The second expectation uses Y independent of all K inputs. Applying NWJ to the augmented variables gives I_alpha<=I(X_1;Y). At alpha=0 this is NWJ after the critic transformation T=1+f−log q; at alpha=1 exchangeability makes the product expectation equal one and yields InfoNCE. For interior alpha the product term must be retained. A leave-one-out minibatch implementation can hold out an additional paired sample’s Y to estimate that independent product term, leaving K other inputs in the normalizer.

claims.statement: Draw X_1:K independently from p(x), with Y conditional on X_1 for the joint term. Let m(y;X_1:K)=K^−1 sum_i exp(f(X_i,y)), b_alpha=alpha*m+(1−alpha)*q(y), and r=exp(f(X_1,y))/b_alpha, for q(y)>0 and alpha in [0,1]. Define I_alpha=1+E_p(x_1:K)p(y|x_1)[log r]−E_p(x_1:K)p(y)[r]. The second expectation uses Y independent of all K inputs. Applying NWJ to the augmented variables gives I_alpha<=I(X_1;Y). At alpha=0 this is NWJ after the critic transformation T=1+f−log q; at alpha=1 exchangeability makes the product expectation equal one and yields InfoNCE. For interior alpha the product term must be retained. A leave-one-out minibatch implementation can hold out an additional paired sample’s Y to estimate that independent product term, leaving K other inputs in the normalizer.

entries.definition: An expectation-level upper bound on mutual information that compares a known conditional density for each paired sample with a mixture of conditional densities from the other independent inputs in its batch.
entries.identity_notes: This is the leave-one-out upper bound in Poole et al., distinct from InfoNCE’s lower bound and from generic leave-one-out cross-validation. It requires evaluable normalized p(y|x), which may be the encoder defining the modeled joint distribution; an arbitrary learned critic does not supply that requirement. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 208 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 57 lines each: existing MINE-f component discussion, shared primary-source references, and discovery/review context. Four native neighbors and seven exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing relations were inspected.
entries.mechanism: Draw K>=2 independent pairs (X_i,Y_i) from p(x)p(y|x), with evaluable normalized conditional density p(y|x). For each i form q_-i(y)=(K−1)^−1 sum_(j!=i) p(y|X_j). Then I(X;Y)<=E[K^−1 sum_i log(p(Y_i|X_i)/q_-i(Y_i))], assuming the expectations are well-defined. The mixture q_-i is independent of the held-out pair because it uses only the other inputs. Conditional on those inputs, the gap of the corresponding variational upper bound is KL(p(Y)||q_-i(Y)), a nonnegative quantity. Including the paired input in this denominator instead gives the known-conditional InfoNCE lower-bound construction, so the exclusion is essential. A finite batch computes an estimator of the upper-bound expectation rather than a guaranteed upper bound on its own.

limitations: The conditional must be normalized and evaluable for cross-sample inputs. Treating an uncalibrated score as p(y|x) invalidates the stated derivation.
For small batches or sharply separated conditional supports, the leave-one-out mixture can be tiny or zero where the held-out conditional is positive, producing a loose or infinite upper bound.
Independence of batch examples is part of the proof. Correlated samples or using the held-out input to construct its own denominator require a different argument.

The expected bound does not certify a realized finite-sample number. Optimization of a noisy estimate does not guarantee monotonic true information reduction or convergence. No encoder implementation or benchmark was reproduced.
